story.iWant: create the basic Jekyll project structure with GitHub Pages compatibility
story.soThat: I have a foundation for the blog with proper configuration and can begin local development
story.tasks: - Task 1: Create Project Structure (15 min) - Task 2: Configure Docker Compose (20 min) - Task 3: Configure Ruby Dependencies (20 min) - Task 4: Configure Jekyll (20 min) - Task 5: Configure Git (10 min) - Task 6: Create Documentation (30 min) - Task 7: Validate Environment (30 min)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
AC-1.1.1: Docker Compose Configuration - docker-compose.yml file created with jekyll/jekyll:3.9 image - docker-compose up successfully starts Jekyll server on port 4000 - LiveReload server accessible on port 35729 - Environment variable JEKYLL_ENV=development configured - Volume mount .:/srv/jekyll configured for file sharing - Command includes --drafts --livereload --host 0.0.0.0 flags
AC-1.1.2: Project Directory Structure - _posts/ directory created for published articles - _drafts/ directory created for unpublished drafts - assets/images/ directory created for article images - _site/ directory excluded from Git (build output) - .jekyll-cache/ directory excluded from Git
AC-1.1.3: Git Configuration - .gitignore file created - .gitignore includes _site/, Gemfile.lock, .jekyll-cache/ - .gitignore includes vendor/bundle and other Jekyll artifacts - Git repository initialized (if not already)
AC-1.1.4: Ruby Dependencies - Gemfile created with Jekyll 3.9.3 dependency - Gemfile includes minima theme (~> 2.5) - Gemfile includes jekyll-feed plugin (~> 0.12) - Gemfile includes jekyll-sitemap plugin (~> 1.4) - Platform-specific gems included (tzinfo for Windows, wdm for Windows file watching)
AC-1.1.5: Jekyll Configuration - _config.yml created with basic site metadata - Site title: "Personal Technical Blog" - Markdown engine: kramdown - Theme: minima - Plugins configured: jekyll-feed, jekyll-sitemap - Exclude list includes Gemfile, node_modules, vendor, .git
AC-1.1.6: Documentation - README.md created with setup instructions - README documents Docker Compose workflow (docker-compose up) - README documents local preview URL (http://localhost:4000) - README explains _drafts vs _posts workflow - README includes troubleshooting section (port conflicts, Docker setup)
AC-1.1.7: Performance Validation - Local environment starts in <30 seconds from docker-compose up command - Jekyll server reports "Server running" message - Browser can access http://localhost:4000 successfully - No errors in Docker Compose logs during startup

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: Docker Compose environment spins up local Jekyll/Hugo instance with live reload on file changes. Preview drafts and published articles locally before merging.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: Docker Compose local preview starts in <30 seconds. Live reload reflects changes in <5 seconds. Static site build completes in <2 minutes for 50 articles.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Simple Jekyll project structure with jekyll/jekyll:3.9 Docker image. Gemfile for GitHub Pages compatibility with github-pages gem, jekyll-feed, and jekyll-seo-tag plugins.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Docker Compose service using jekyll/jekyll:3.9 image with command 'jekyll serve --drafts --livereload --host 0.0.0.0'. Ports 4000 (server) and 35729 (LiveReload) exposed with volume mount to /srv/jekyll.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Directory structure includes _posts/ for published articles, _drafts/ for unpublished, assets/images/ for media, _site/ for build output (gitignored), and scripts/ for automation.

doc.title: Architecture Document

doc.title: Epic 1 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Configuration includes site metadata (title, description, email), markdown: kramdown, theme: minima, plugins (jekyll-feed, jekyll-sitemap), and exclude list for Gemfile, node_modules, vendor.

doc.snippet: Gemfile with Jekyll ~> 3.9.3, minima ~> 2.5, jekyll-feed ~> 0.12, jekyll-sitemap ~> 1.4 in plugins group. Platform-specific gems for Windows (tzinfo, wdm).

doc.title: Epic 1 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Acceptance criteria specifies docker-compose.yml creation, successful startup on port 4000, LiveReload on 35729, directory structure (_posts/, _drafts/, assets/images/), .gitignore setup, and <30 second startup time.

gem.name: jekyll
gem.purpose: Static site generator, GitHub Pages compatible

image.name: jekyll/jekyll
image.purpose: Official Jekyll Docker image with Ruby and dependencies pre-installed

story-context.constraints: - MUST use Jekyll 3.9.3 for GitHub Pages native compatibility (ADR-001) - MUST use default Minima theme (no customization for MVP) - Docker Compose environment must match production GitHub Pages build - All content must be pure markdown with YAML front matter - Jekyll version pinned to ~> 3.9.3 in Gemfile - Docker image must be jekyll/jekyll:3.9 (specific tag, not latest) - Local environment must work cross-platform (macOS, Linux, Windows) - Performance: Docker Compose startup <30 seconds (NFR-1) - Performance: Live reload cycle <5 seconds (NFR-1) - File naming: Articles must follow YYYY-MM-DD-title.md format - Git: _site/, Gemfile.lock, .jekyll-cache/ must be excluded - No secrets in _config.yml or committed files
story-context.interfaces: - Jekyll CLI: jekyll build, jekyll serve, jekyll clean - Docker Compose CLI: docker-compose up, docker-compose down - Jekyll server: http://localhost:4000 (main server) - LiveReload WebSocket: ws://localhost:35729 (auto-refresh) - File system: Input from _posts/ and _drafts/, output to _site/

tests.standards: Epic 1 is foundational infrastructure with manual validation for all acceptance criteria. No automated testing for local development setup. Test approach includes: environment setup testing, configuration testing, content authoring testing, workflow testing, and performance testing. All tests are manual validation with clear success criteria defined in the tech spec.
tests.locations: N/A - This story involves infrastructure setup only. Future stories will add tests in standard Jekyll/Ruby locations.
tests.ideas: - AC-1.1.1: Manual test - Run docker-compose up and verify server starts within 30 seconds on port 4000 - AC-1.1.1: Manual test - Verify LiveReload accessible on port 35729 via browser DevTools - AC-1.1.2: Manual test - Verify all directories created (_posts/, _drafts/, assets/images/) - AC-1.1.3: Manual test - Verify .gitignore excludes _site/ and .jekyll-cache/ (run git status to confirm) - AC-1.1.4: Manual test - Verify Gemfile syntax is valid Ruby and contains all required gems - AC-1.1.5: Manual test - Verify _config.yml YAML syntax is valid and Jekyll builds successfully - AC-1.1.6: Manual test - Follow README instructions from scratch to verify completeness - AC-1.1.7: Performance test - Measure startup time from docker-compose up to "Server running" message (must be <30 seconds) - Error case test - Start another service on port 4000 and verify clear error message about port conflict - Cross-platform test - Test on macOS, Linux, and/or Windows (if available)
